disclosure_text: I am an immigrant who came to Canada as a student for further mu education, so immigration has been a major challenge i have  faced since i moved here trying to maintain residency and also from the minority group.
micronarrative:
In 2022 and 2023, Canada welcomed a record number of international students, and the influx brought with it a wave of concerns about housing, rising costs, and low-wage jobs. As a citizen, I felt the pressure firsthand. In my community, there were banners and local resources, but the reality was that the strain on housing and healthcare was palpable. Some people felt that immigrants were to blame, while others believed the federal government needed better planning.

I noticed that my communication style had to change depending on the group I was speaking to. With locals, I spoke more slowly, avoided large words, and paid more attention to body language and tone. With more diverse groups, I had to become more direct and balanced. This experience definitely polished how I communicated with different groups. It taught me that effective communication is not just about speaking the same language but also understanding people's emotions and backgrounds.

I had to become more adaptable with my words, recognizing that people view situations differently. Now, I approach conversations with more openness and flexibility, listening carefully without making assumptions. This has made me a more empathetic and effective communicator.
